title: CustomDomainConnect
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.foundation.layout.Column of MonarchTextField, MonarchButton, MonarchDomainProgress and MonarchDnsRecordTable; MonarchDialog to confirm removal
summary: A recipe, not a component: enter a custom domain, add the DNS records it needs with copy buttons, verify them, follow the progress to live, and remove the domain.
whenToUse: In settings where a customer connects their own domain to a help center, a booking page or a website.
whenNotToUse: To only show DNS records, use MonarchDnsRecordTable. To only show the progress of a domain, use MonarchDomainProgress.
api: MonarchTextField(value = typed, onValueChange = { … }, label = "Domain", errorText = error, keyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions(keyboardType = KeyboardType.Uri))
MonarchDnsRecordTable(records = listOf(MonarchDnsRecord("CNAME", domain, "domains.example.net", MonarchDnsRecordPurpose.Routing, found = false)))

options.name: domain
options.description: The connected domain, from the app's state; null shows the entry step.

options.name: stage
options.description: Where the domain is: DNS, ownership, certificate, page or live, from the app's server.

options.name: records
options.description: The records to add, from the server, each with found once it is seen.

options.name: verifying
options.description: While a check runs, the verify button shows progress.

states.name: enter
states.description: The domain field with its error and Connect domain.

states.name: records
states.description: The domain as a heading with Remove domain, MonarchDomainProgress, the records to add and Verify DNS.

states.name: verifying
states.description: Verify DNS shows progress; MonarchDomainProgress shows the stage.

states.name: live
states.description: MonarchDomainProgress shows the domain as live; the app may hide the records.

states.name: remove
states.description: A MonarchDialog confirms; the entry step comes back.

appearance: Every part is an existing Monarch component: the text field, the domain progress steps, the record cards or table with copy buttons, and buttons, on the canvas. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.
platformNotes: The web's CustomDomainConnect is one component with a Stepper, a form, a status line, a records table, a provider hint select and a confirm dialog. On Android it is a recipe from MonarchDomainProgress (the steps and the status), MonarchDnsRecordTable (cards on a phone, a table on wide screens) and MonarchTextField and MonarchButton, with a MonarchDialog to confirm removal. The web's provider hints are text the app shows under the records, for example in a MonarchCollapsible. The web's domain syntax checks are the app's validation before it calls its server. iOS has the same plan: a recipe.
accessibility: The domain field has a visible label and its error is set as the field's error.
MonarchDomainProgress reads each step with its state; MonarchDnsRecordTable names each copy button with the record.
Remove is confirmed in a MonarchDialog, which TalkBack reads as a dialog.
edgeCases: Normalise the typed domain (trim, lower case, no trailing dot) before sending it.
DNS can take hours: let people leave and come back; keep the records visible until the domain is live.
The server stays the authority on whether a record is found.
